newsitem.title: USA: Genzyme unit participating in cancer study.
newsitem.headline: Genzyme unit participating in cancer study.

text.p: Genzyme Corp said Thursday its genetic diagnostics unit's technology will be used in a colon cancer study.
The technology, known as multiplex allele-specific diagnostic assay, will be used in a study being conducted by Kaiser Permanente and the University of California at San Francisco.
The technology will be used to detect mutations associated with hereditary non-polyposis colorectal cancer in patient samples, the company said.

The study is designed to determine the role that abnormalities play in a class of genes known to be associated with the development of early-onset colorectal cancer. All of the patients taking part in the study will have been diagnosed with the cancer before turning 35.
It is hoped the study will lead to ways to diagnose the cancer at an earlier stage, when it can be more successfully treated.
